Great. Here’s a structured 12-week strength program for a 27-year-old beginner with only a yoga mat and a doorway pull-up bar. The plan progresses from foundational movement patterns to more demanding exercises, focusing on full-body strength, steady progression, and sustainable recovery. Each week includes 3 primary strength sessions and optional 2 lighter or technique-focused sessions. All workouts use bodyweight and the doorway pull-up bar; when appropriate, we’ll add a simple tempo or isometric hold to increase time under tension.

Assumptions
- Training 4 days per week (e.g., Mon, Tue, Thu, Sat) with at least 1 rest day between upper/lower splits; or adjust to 3 days if needed (e.g., Mon/Wed/Fri) but Week 1–4 are written for 4 days.
- Warm-up included before each session: 5–8 minutes of light cardio/mobility plus 1–2 warm-up sets.
- Progression: increase difficulty by tempo change, range of motion, added holds, or adding reps before loading; never sacrifice form.
- Pull-up bar use: start with holds and eccentric work if full pull-ups aren’t yet possible.

Program structure
- Phases:
  - Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Foundation and technique (unilateral balance, push/pull patterns, hips/core).
  - Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Strength building with progressive volume and tempo; introduce more demanding variations.
  - Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Advanced strength and muscle-building emphasis with higher tolerances, added isometrics, and objective progression.

Weekly overview (three main strength sessions per week; add optional mobility/conditioning days if desired)
- Session A: Push emphasis (chest/shoulders/triceps) + core
- Session B: Pull emphasis (back/biceps) + core
- Session C: Legs/hips/glutes + posterior chain + core
- Optional: Mobility/conditioning days or light technique days to work on form or cardio.

Important notes about equipment
- Doorway pull-up bar: perform all pull-up/push-up variations using the bar as appropriate. If you cannot yet perform a standard pull-up, start with pull-up progressions (inverted rows under a door frame, hanging knee raises, eccentric-only pull-ups, isometric holds at top/bottom of the movement, towel-assisted variations). Use the bar for vertical pulling as you progress.
- No weights; use tempo, reps, and time under tension to increase difficulty. You can also perform isometric holds at peak contraction to increase difficulty.

Week-by-week plan

Phase 1: Foundation and technique (Weeks 1–4)
Goals: Build movement awareness, establish baseline strength, learn proper form, and prepare tendons for higher loads.

Week 1
- Session A (Push)
  - Warm-up: 5–8 minutes dynamic mobility (shoulders, chest, wrists), 1–2 minutes of light cardio (marching or jogging in place)
  - Push-ups (knee or incline if needed): 3 sets x 6–8 reps (focus on full ROM)
  - Incline push-ups on doorway bar or high shelf: 3 x 6–8
  - Dips assisted at bar (feet on ground or elevated): 3 x 4–6
  - Plank: 3 x 20–30 seconds
  - Finisher: Wall handstand progressions or scapular push-ups 2 x 8–10
- Session B (Pull)
  - Warm-up: 5–8 minutes, scapular retraction and opening
  - Inverted rows beneath doorway bar: 3 x 6–8
  - Doorway pull-ups (assisted or negative): 3 x 3–5
  - Bar hang (dead hang or hang with bent knees): 3 x 15–20 seconds
  - Bicep isometric hold on bar: 2 x 15 seconds
- Session C (Legs/Core)
  - Warm-up: hip hinge/lunges mobility
  - Bodyweight squats: 3 x 8–12
  - Bulgarian split squat (use chair for rear leg): 3 x 6–8 per leg
  - Glute bridge on mat: 3 x 12–15
  - Romanian deadlift with hip hinge (no weight): 3 x 8–10
  - Lying leg raises: 3 x 10–12

Week 2
- Increase by 1 rep per set if comfortable; keep form strict.
- Session A
  - Push-ups: 3 x 8–10
  - Incline push-ups: 3 x 8–10
  - Dips (assisted): 3 x 5–6
  - Plank: 3 x 30–40 seconds
  - Scapular push-ups: 2 x 10
- Session B
  - Inverted rows: 3 x 7–9
  - Pull-ups (assisted/negatives): 3 x 4–6
  - Dead hang: 3 x 20–25 seconds
  - Bar hangs with chin tucked: 2 x 20 seconds
- Session C
  - Squats: 3 x 9–12
  - Split squats: 3 x 8–10 per leg
  - Glute bridges: 3 x 14–18
  - Romanian deadlift (bodyweight): 3 x 8–10
  - Bicycle crunches: 3 x 12–16 per side

Week 3
- Start adding tempo to push and pull movements (2–0–2 tempo for eccentric, 1–2 seconds pause at bottom)
- Session A
  - Push-ups: 3 x 8–12 with 2-second eccentric
  - Incline push-ups: 3 x 9–12
  - Dips: 3 x 6–8
  - Plank: 3 x 45 seconds
  - Scapular push-ups: 2 x 12
- Session B
  - Inverted rows: 3 x 8–10
  - Pull-ups: 3 x 5–6 (negatives or assisted)
  - Dead hang: 3 x 25–30 seconds
  - Isometric hold at top of pull-up: 2 x 10 seconds
- Session C
  - Squats: 3 x 10–12
  - Step-ups (use a sturdy chair): 3 x 8–10 per leg
  - Glute bridges: 3 x 15–20
  - Romanian deadlift (single-leg RDL progressions if possible): 3 x 6–8 per leg
  - Reverse crunches: 3 x 12–15

Week 4
- Deload style progression with continued technique refinement
- Session A
  - Push-ups: 3 x 10–14
  - Incline push-ups: 3 x 10–12
  - Dips: 3 x 6–8
  - Plank: 3 x 50–60 seconds
  - Scapular push-ups: 2 x 12–15
- Session B
  - Inverted rows: 3 x 9–11
  - Pull-ups/assisted: 3 x 5–7
  - Dead hang: 3 x 30 seconds
  - Top-isometric hold: 2 x 12 seconds
- Session C
  - Squats: 3 x 12–15
  - Split squats: 3 x 8–10 per leg
  - Glute bridges: 3 x 18–22
  - Hip hinge to toe touch (good mornings, light): 3 x 10
  - Plank with leg lift: 2 x 12 per leg

Phase 2: Strength building and progression (Weeks 5–8)
Goals: Increase volume and introduce more challenging versions; emphasize control and full ROM.

Week 5
- Session A
  - Push-ups: 4 x 8–12 (add a 2-second bottom hold)
  - Diamond push-ups (hands near bar): 3 x 6–8 or regular push-ups if needed
  - Dips: 3 x 6–8
  - Plank: 3 x 60 seconds
  - Scapular push-ups: 2 x 12
- Session B
  - Inverted rows: 4 x 8–10
  - Pull-ups/assisted: 3 x 6–8
  - Dead hang: 3 x 35 seconds
  - Isometric hold at top: 2 x 12 seconds
- Session C
  - Squats: 4 x 12–15
  - Split squats: 3 x 8–10 per leg
  - Glute bridges: 3 x 20
  - Hip hinge to toe touch: 3 x 12
  - Side plank: 2 x 20–30 seconds per side

Week 6
- Session A
  - Push-ups: 4 x 9–12
  - Incline push-ups: 3 x 10–12
  - Dips: 3 x 7–9
  - Plank: 3 x 70 seconds
  - Scapular push-ups: 2 x 12–15
- Session B
  - Inverted rows: 4 x 9–11
  - Pull-ups/assisted: 3 x 6–8
  - Dead hang: 3 x 40 seconds
  - Top hold: 2 x 15 seconds
- Session C
  - Squats: 4 x 12–16
  - Step-ups: 3 x 10 per leg
  - Glute bridges single-leg: 3 x 10 per leg (if possible; otherwise 2 x 12)
  - Romanian deadlift (bodyweight with tempo): 3 x 10
  - Bicycle crunches: 3 x 16 per side

Week 7
- Introduce tempo and pause reps to increase time under tension
- Session A
  - Push-ups: 4 x 10–14 with 2-second pause at bottom
  - Diamond push-ups: 3 x 6–9
  - Dips: 3 x 7–9
  - Plank: 3 x 75 seconds
  - Scapular push-ups: 2 x 15
- Session B
  - Inverted rows: 4 x 10–12
  - Pull-ups/assisted: 3 x 6–8
  - Dead hang: 3 x 45 seconds
  - Top hold: 2 x 18 seconds
- Session C
  - Squats: 4 x 14–18
  - Split squats: 3 x 9–11 per leg
  - Glute bridges: 3 x 22
  - Hip hinge to toe touch: 3 x 12
  - Side crunches: 3 x 12 per side

Week 8
- Peak week for phase 2; push for higher reps and flow
- Session A
  - Push-ups: 4 x 12–16
  - Incline push-ups: 3 x 12–15
  - Dips: 3 x 8–10
  - Plank: 3 x 90 seconds
  - Scapular push-ups: 2 x 15
- Session B
  - Inverted rows: 4 x 11–13
  - Pull-ups/assisted: 3 x 6–9
  - Dead hang: 3 x 50 seconds
  - Top hold: 2 x 20 seconds
- Session C
  - Squats: 4 x 15–20
  - Step-ups or walking lunges (if space): 3 x 10–12 per leg
  - Glute bridges: 3 x 24
  - Romanian deadlift: 3 x 12
  - Plank to side plank transitions: 3 x 6 per side

Phase 3: Advanced strength emphasis and conditioning (Weeks 9–12)
Goals: Increase absolute strength capacity and consistency; introduce tighter progression and more demanding core work.

Week 9
- Session A
  - Push-ups: 4 x 12–16 with 3-second eccentric
  - Dips: 3 x 8–10
  - Pike push-ups (shoulder emphasis) or elevated feet push-ups: 3 x 6–8
  - Plank: 3 x 90 seconds
  - Scapular push-ups: 2 x 15
- Session B
  - Pull-ups: 3 x 6–8
  - Inverted rows: 3 x 10–12
  - Dead hang: 3 x 60 seconds
  - Isometric hold at top: 2 x 18 seconds
- Session C
  - Squats: 4 x 16–20
  - Split squats: 3 x 10–12 per leg
  - Glute bridges: 3 x 24–28
  - Hip hinge to toe touch: 3 x 14
  - Ab wheel substitute: if no wheel, V-ups: 3 x 12

Week 10
- Session A
  - Push-ups: 4 x 14–18
  - Dips: 3 x 9–11
  - Pike push-ups: 3 x 6–9
  - Plank: 3 x 100 seconds
  - Scapular push-ups: 2 x 16
- Session B
  - Pull-ups: 3 x 7–9
  - Inverted rows: 3 x 11–13
  - Dead hang: 3 x 65 seconds
  - Top hold: 2 x 20 seconds
- Session C
  - Squats: 4 x 18–22
  - Step-ups or walking lunges: 3 x 12–14 per leg
  - Glute bridges: 3 x 26–30
  - Romanian deadlift: 3 x 12
  - Side plank with hip dips: 3 x 12 per side

Week 11
- Increase intensity through tempo and control
- Session A
  - Push-ups: 4 x 12–16 with 3-second bottom pause
  - Dips: 3 x 9–11
  - Pike push-ups: 3 x 7–9
  - Plank: 3 x 110 seconds
  - Scapular push-ups: 2 x 18
- Session B
  - Pull-ups: 3 x 7–9 (aim for unassisted if possible)
  - Inverted rows: 3 x 12–14
  - Dead hang: 3 x 70 seconds
  - Top hold: 2 x 22 seconds
- Session C
  - Squats: 4 x 20–24
  - Split squats: 3 x 11–13 per leg
  - Glute bridges: 3 x 28–32
  - Hip hinge to toe touch: 3 x 14
  - Abdominal circuit: 3 rounds (bicycle 20 per side, leg raises 12, flutter kicks 20 seconds)

Week 12
- Final week to test progress and consolidate gains
- Session A
  - Push-ups: 4 x 14–18
  - Dips: 3 x 10–12
  - Pike push-ups: 3 x 8–10
  - Plank: 3 x 120 seconds
  - Scapular push-ups: 2 x 20
- Session B
  - Pull-ups: 3 x 8–10 (unassist as possible)
  - Inverted rows: 3 x 13–15
  - Dead hang: 3 x 75 seconds
  - Top hold: 2 x 25 seconds
- Session C
  - Squats: 4 x 22–26
  - Step-ups/WL lunges: 3 x 12–14 per leg
  - Glute bridges: 3 x 30
  - Hip hinge to toe touch: 3 x 16
  - Core finisher: 3 rounds (front plank 60 seconds, side planks 30 seconds each side, hollow body hold 20 seconds)

Recovery and nutrition guidance
- Sleep: Aim for 7–9 hours per night; quality matters for recovery.
- Protein: Target about 1.6–2.2 g/kg body weight daily to support muscle repair. Distribute across meals (e.g., 25–40 g protein per meal, 3–4 meals/day).
- Hydration: 2–3 liters daily, more on training days.
- Nutrition timing: If appetite allows, have a protein-rich meal or shake within 1–2 hours post-workout.
- General guidance: Balanced meals with lean proteins, whole grains, vegetables, and healthy fats. If weight gain is desired, create a small caloric surplus (150–300 kcal/day); if fat loss is desired, a small deficit (−300 kcal/day) can be considered while maintaining protein intake.
- For bodyweight training with limited equipment, nutrition should focus on adequate protein and energy for workouts. Avoid large meals immediately before heavy sessions; 1–2 hours prior is reasonable.

Recovery practices
- Mobility: 5–10 minutes post-workout focusing on hips, thoracic spine, shoulders, and ankles.
- Deloads: The Week 4 and Week 8 transitions are light deload-style weeks; you can do optional lighter sessions if you feel fatigued.
- Soft tissue work: Gentle self-massage or rolling on major muscle groups if fascia stiffness is present (forearms, lats, glutes, quads).
- Injury management: If pain is sharp or joint-altering, reduce range of motion and volume; consult a clinician if pain persists.

Progression notes
- If any week becomes too easy, add reps by 1–2 or reduce rest between sets (down to 60–90 seconds). If you stall for 2–3 weeks, increase difficulty by:
  - Increasing tempo or pause durations (e.g., 3-second eccentric, 1-second pause at bottom)
  - Adding extra range of motion (declined push-ups, deeper squats)
  - Adding an additional set (e.g., 4th set on main lifts)
  - Transition to more challenging variations (e.g., regular to elevated feet push-ups, incline to decline or pike push-ups)
- If space or time is limited, you can compress to 3 days per week using full-body workouts with one main push, pull, and legs exercise per session. The progression logic should remain the same.

Safety reminders
- Prioritize form over volume. If a movement causes pain (not muscle fatigue), stop and switch to a regression.
- Maintain a stable core and neutral spine during all exercises.
- For pull movements, engage scapular retraction and avoid excessive kipping or swinging.

If you’d like, I can tailor the exact weekly days, adjust rep schemes to fit your client’s schedule, or convert this into a printable calendar with daily notes.
